exercises.heading: 4.1. Exercises

problem.paragraph: Explain the difference between an absolute minimum and a local minimum.

solution.paragraph: Abs min: smallest function value on the entire domain of the function; loc min at $$c$$ : smallest function value when $$x$$ is near $$c$$

problem.paragraph: Suppose $$f$$ is a continuous function defined on a closed interval $$\left\lbrack {a,b} \right\rbrack$$ .

list.item: What theorem guarantees the existence of an absolute maximum value and an absolute minimum value for $$f$$ ?
What steps would you take to find those maximum and minimum values?

exercises.instruction: 3–4 For each of the numbers $$a$$ , $$b$$ , $$c$$ , $$d$$ , $$r$$ , and $$s$$ , state whether the function whose graph is shown has an absolute maximum or minimum, a local maximum or minimum, or neither a maximum nor a minimum.

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed with tick marks a, b, c, d, r, and s, in the order from left to right at irregular intervals. The curve begins at x = a, goes down and to the right, concave down, reaches a sharp low point at x = b, a little away from the x axis, then goes up and to the right, concave down, reaches its high point at x = c, goes down and to the right, and inflects at x = d. After inflection, the curve then goes down and to the right, becoming concave up, reaches its low point near the x axis at x = r, then goes up and to the right, now concave down, and exits with a high point at x = s. The exit point of the graph is a little higher than that of the high point at x = c. Vertical line segments from each of the tick marks reach the curve.

solution.paragraph: Abs max at $$s$$ , abs min at $$r$$ , loc max at $$c$$ , loc min at $$b$$ and $$r$$ , neither a max nor a min at $$a$$ and $$d$$

image.alt: Details A curve with three disconnected parts is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed with tick marks a, b, c, d, r, and s in the order from left to right at irregular intervals. The first part begins at x = a with a solid dot, goes up and to the right, concave down, and ends at x = b with a solid dot. The second part begins at x = b with an open dot, a little above the x axis, goes up and to the right, concave down, and ends at x = c with an open dot. The third part begins at x = c with a solid dot, goes down and to the right, concave up, reaches its low point at x = d, then goes up and to the right to a sharp high point at x = r. It then goes down and to the right, again concave up, and ends at x = s with a solid dot.

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 1 to 7 in increments of 1 unit. The y axis is displayed from negative 1 to 6 in increments of 1 unit. The curve y = f(x) has two parts. The first part begins at the point (0, 2) with a solid dot, goes up and to the right, concave down, reaches its high point with an open dot at (1, 4), then goes down and to the right, concave up, and reaches its low point at (2, 2). It then goes up and to the right through (3, 4), concave down, reaches its high point at (4, 5), then goes down and to the right, and reaches its sharp low point at (5, 3), and then goes up and to the right, concave down, and ends at the point (6, 4) with a solid dot. There is a solid dot at (1, 3). The second part begins at the point (6, 3) with an open dot, goes down and to the right, concave down, and ends at (7, 1) with an open dot.

Details A curve is graphed in the first quadrant of the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is displayed from negative 1 to 7 in increments of 1 unit. The y axis is displayed from negative 1 to 6 in increments of 1 unit. There is a solid dot at (2, 2).

problem.paragraph: When a foreign object lodged in the trachea forces a person to cough, the diaphragm thrusts upward, causing an increase in pressure in the lungs. This is accompanied by a contraction of the trachea, making a narrower channel for the expelled air to flow through. For a given amount of air to escape in a fixed time, it must move faster through the narrower channel than the wider one. The greater the velocity of the airstream, the greater the force on the foreign object. X-rays show that the radius of the circular tracheal tube contracts to about two-thirds of its normal radius during a cough. According to a mathematical model of coughing, the velocity $$v$$ of the airstream is related to the radius $$r$$ of the trachea by the equation

where $$k$$ is a constant and $$r_{0}$$ is the normal radius of the trachea. The restriction on $$r$$ is due to the fact that the tracheal wall stiffens under pressure and a contraction greater than $$\frac{1}{2}r_{0}$$ is prevented (otherwise the person would suffocate).

list.item: Determine the value of $$r$$ in the interval $$\left\lbrack {\frac{1}{2}r_{0},r_{0}} \right\rbrack$$ at which $$\upsilon$$ has an absolute maximum. How does this compare with experimental evidence?
What is the absolute maximum value of $$v$$ on the interval?
Sketch the graph of $$v$$ on the interval $$\left\lbrack {0,r_{0}} \right\rbrack$$ .

problem.paragraph: A cubic function is a polynomial of degree $$3$$ ; that is, it has the form $$f(x) = ax^{3} + bx^{2} + cx + d$$ , where $$a \neq 0$$ .

list.item: Show that a cubic function can have two, one, or no critical number(s). Give examples and sketches to illustrate the three possibilities.
How many local extreme values can a cubic function have?
